Subject: Implementation validation questionnaire + proposed migration sequence — Aquila Systems

Hi Maria,

Attached is our completed implementation validation questionnaire and an initial migration sequence for Aquila Systems (Aquila_RFP_answers_v1.pdf; migration-timeline-proposal.xlsx). Highlights below so you can scan quickly: 

- Staging integration: 2-week integration window with two full regression runs (smoke + perf).
- Canary plan: 3-step traffic shift (1% -> 10% -> 50%) with 24h observability gates and automated rollback triggers on error rate or latency regression.
- Data residency & KMS: We'll deploy a private control plane in the eu-west-1 region and support KMS envelope encryption (bring-your-own-key supported).
- Cutover weekend: recommended Saturday 02:00–06:00 CET; we include a fallback window and script to revert routing.
- Acceptance criteria: successful end-to-end verification tests (5 predefined transactions), zero P0 errors for 4 hours post-shift, and telemetry parity between staging/production.

Please review and let us know the three items we need to firm up from your side: network peering CIDR, database maintenance window constraints, and any additional compliance evidence procurement needs. Happy to walk through the runbook on a call — propose next Tue or Wed.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Jonas — thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments (reviewing now). A few clarifying questions from our side: 

1) EU-specific SLAs: can you confirm the latency SLOs we should expect for the eu-west deployment when serving 99th percentile during normal traffic? Our network team needs a numbers table they can sign off on.

2) DB cutover: the migration-timeline spreadsheet lists a DB sync but not the verification tests. Can you provide the exact test scripts/queries you run to verify data fidelity? How long do they typically take for a 400GB dataset?

3) KMS & audit logs: procurement will want to see where audit logs are retained and for how long — SOC2 evidence would help. Can you share a pointer to the audit retention policy and sample log extracts?

4) Can we avoid any downtime for the matching service? If not, what's the expected outage window?

Also, can you include an explicit runbook snippet for the 1%->10% gating step — especially the telemetry thresholds (error rate, tail latency, token-quality regression) that trigger auto-rollback?

I'll loop in the network and procurement owners after your answers. Proposed call: Tue 8 Dec at 10:00 CET — does that work?

Best,
Maria Garcia
Program Manager, Integrations | Aquila Systems

Maria — thanks for the precise questions. I've inline-answered below and attached a focused runbook (AQ-migration-runbook-v2.docx) plus a staging validation checklist (.csv) that maps each acceptance test to owner and elapsed time estimates. Summary answers first, details inline: 

Summary (short):
- 99th percentile eu-west SLO: 220ms for text-generation endpoints under baseline load (95th percentile of expected load). We include per-route baselining in the runbook and a contingency to route to a lower-latency variant if breached.
- DB verification: we run row-count parity, checksums, and sample-consistency queries. For ~400GB of active data the verification suite completes in ~50–90 minutes depending on parallelism and available read replicas; plan allocates a 2-hour window for buffer.
- KMS & audit logs: audit logs retained in the customer's S3 bucket for 365 days by default; SOC2 artifacts and a sample log bundle are attached (see shared drive link).
- Matching service: designed for zero-downtime shadow cutover; we recommend a staged traffic shadowing + compare phase to avoid any outage — fallback is immediate DNS reroute if inconsistency detected.

Inline details: 
> 1) EU-specific SLAs — see runbook §2.1 and table on page 3. 99th pctl numbers reflect baseline tests; we will run an on-site (virtual) load validation ahead of go-live and sign-off with you.

> 2) DB cutover — runbook §3.2 lists the exact verification queries and the automation wrapper we use; included is an estimate for run time and parallelization knobs.

> 3) KMS & audit logs — we will provide a SOC2 snapshot and redact-only audit extracts for procurement review; logs are stored in your S3 with restricted IAM. See link: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/AQ/runbook-v2

> 4) 1%->10% gating metrics — automated gates are: error rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m, 99th pctl latency delta > 40% vs baseline for 10m, or token-level quality regression > 3% on the prompt sample set. Any gate failure triggers automatic rollback and a P0 page to the on-call team (contacts in runbook).

Proposed next steps:
- We will finalize runbook v2 and send a redlined version by EOD today (attached).
- Confirm Tue 8 Dec 10:00 CET is OK for a 45 min run-through + procurement attendance.
- Please send network CIDR and preferred maintenance window by Mon 7 Dec.

Attaching: AQ-migration-runbook-v2.docx (docx), staging-validation-checklist.csv (csv)

Regards,
Laura Bennett
